title: Agreeing When Messages Run Late — The Foot of Mount Phyle
description: Dwork, Lynch and Stockmeyer's partial synchrony: four mercenaries and their ravens stay safe in any wind, and commit once the wind drops, though none can tell when it did.
question: If messages can run late without limit, agreement cannot be guaranteed; yet real networks are prompt most of the time. Can a protocol stay safe however late messages run, and still decide once they arrive on time again?
how: We find out by exploring how the same Greek mercenaries, on a windy night when no one could tell how long a raven would take, agreed whether to attack or hold once the wind had dropped.

papers.authors: Cynthia Dwork, Nancy Lynch and Larry Stockmeyer
papers.title: Consensus in the Presence of Partial Synchrony
